tagline.text: An April festival that re-stages Lapulapu's 1521 victory on the beach at Mactan

location.label: Location
location.text: Mactan Shrine (Liberty Shrine) area, Barangay Mactan, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,000 (one day of viewing, transport and meals; lodging not included)

children.text: Kadaugan sa Mactan is Lapu-Lapu City's annual festival commemorating the victory of Lapulapu's warriors over Magellan's expedition at the Battle of Mactan on April 27, 1521. Food festivals and performances run through the month of April, and the battle is reenacted on the beach in front of the Mactan Shrine on the 27th.

"Kadaugan" means "victory" in Cebuano. The festival commemorates the day, April 27, 1521, when the warriors of the chieftain Lapulapu defeated the Spanish expedition led by the Portuguese-born explorer Ferdinand Magellan on the shore of Mactan Island. Wikipedia describes the Battle of Mactan as one of the earliest acts of resistance by Filipinos against foreign rule and calls Lapulapu the "first Filipino national hero." The event is marked every April in Lapu-Lapu City.

The account of the battle that the reenactment revives goes like this. According to Pigafetta's chronicle, as summarized on Wikipedia, Magellan landed with 49 of about 60 Europeans, and the Mactan side is put at about 1,500 warriors. A reef kept the ships' cannon and muskets from reaching the shore, and when Magellan had houses burned, the defenders grew even angrier. Magellan was struck in the leg by a poisoned arrow, fell, and was killed. The surviving members of the expedition returned to Cebu, and in 1522 Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the first circumnavigation of the globe. Numbers differ by source.

The centerpiece is the battle reenactment on the morning of April 27 at the Mactan Shrine (locally also called the Liberty Shrine). A wreath-laying ceremony comes first, then actors playing Lapulapu, Reyna Bulakna (said to be Lapulapu's wife) and Magellan act out the fight by the sea. The reenactment ends with Magellan falling to a sword. Because the city organizes it, there is no admission charge and anyone can watch from the shore.

The festivities do not end in a day but run through April. In 2023 they included documentary screenings, a job fair, cooking demonstrations and a cooking competition, a food festival, concerts and an inter-school cultural contest from April 1 to the end of the month. In 2025 the festival opened on April 4 with a "Food, Fashion and Festivities" kickoff joined by 49 barangays and continued through April 30. The program differs a little every year, so check the city's official announcements for the year you plan to visit. Press reports say the festival began in the late 1970s or early 1980s under the name "Bahug-Bahug sa Mactan" and was renamed "Kadaugan sa Mactan" in 2001 under Mayor Arturo Radaza; the reported starting year differs between 1979 and 1981. In 2026 it marked its 505th anniversary. For a sense of scale, a 2024 report said about 8,000–10,000 people gathered, and the city's 2025 budget was reported at about 12.4 million pesos. In 2026, because of an energy crisis, the city cancelled the street-dance and ritual competitions and cut the production cost from about 3 million pesos to 1.8 million pesos; police estimated the crowd at about 2,500.
On the morning of April 27, actors perform the battle between Lapulapu's warriors and Magellan's expedition on the beach. In 2016 it ran for about
45 minutes

, and in 2025 the former boxer Manny Pacquiao played Lapulapu, which drew attention. In 2026 Elcid Camacho played Lapulapu, Akiko Solon played Reyna Bulakna and Veanz Matutinao played Magellan, and the performers carried national flags and a globe to stress peace.

Before the reenactment, the mayor and government officials lay wreaths in front of the Lapulapu statue. In 2016 there was a morning Mass and a 21-gun salute by the Air Force, and in 2026 the mayor led the wreath-laying.

At the Liberty Shrine, a food festival of about a week serves dishes from hotels and resorts as well as food from local small businesses. In 2023 it was tied to a cooking competition, and in 2026 it was kept going despite the scaling back.

Barangays and schools compete in costume in a street-dance contest. In 2025 all 30 barangays, including Olango Island, took part. In 2026 it was cancelled because of the energy crisis. In 2016 the Rampada contest was held at the Hoops Dome, where Babag won the grand prize and ₱200,000. Ten barangays and seven open-category teams competed.

A pageant modeled on Lapulapu's wife, Reyna Bulakna, has been held during the festival, and a role of the same name appears in the battle reenactment. Check local announcements to see whether it is part of this year's schedule.
In 2023, plans were announced for eskrima practitioners aged 6 to 92 to attempt a Guinness record with an arnis kata. It is a rare chance to see Cebu's traditional martial arts.

Stages with concerts, acoustic nights and talent contests follow one another every night of festival week. In 2023 an SMB Street Party was also held on the night of April 27. That year there was also a Bisrock concert on April 22, a Lapu-Lapu talent contest on the 26th and a car show on the 29th and 30th.

items.title: April 27 day plan
items.subtitle: Watching the reenactment and a loop around Mactan

children.text: Leave from downtown Cebu or your Mactan lodging. In 2016 the roads to Punta Engaño were closed from 7 a.m. A taxi or Grab may have to drop you well short of the shrine entrance.
Arrive at the shrine and first look around the Lapulapu statue and the Magellan marker. It is a good time for photos before the crowds arrive.
Find a shaded spot on the beach side before the ceremony and wreath-laying begin.
Watch the battle reenactment. This was the start time in 2016 and it varies by year, so check local announcements.
After the reenactment, have lunch at the food festival booths.
Move to a beach resort or café on Mactan Island and rest.
Return to downtown Cebu and visit Magellan's Cross and the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño.
Operating hours and road closures change every year, so check the Lapu-Lapu City official page on the morning of the event.
On a festival-week evening, drop by the food festival at the Liberty Shrine and browse the booths.
In 2023 the food festival opened on April 21 with a resort night. Cooking competitions and demonstrations are sometimes held in the daytime, so check the previous day's schedule.
Watch that day's stage show (a concert, acoustic night, talent contest and so on).
Return to your Mactan lodging or downtown Cebu.
The weekly program differs every year and is announced day by day, as in the 2023 schedule.
A direct flight from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes
. April is peak season, so fares rise early.
The airport is on Mactan Island, so you can reach the shrine without leaving the island.

items.title: From the airport to the Mactan Shrine

children.text: The shrine is in Barangay Mactan, toward Punta Engaño. Take a taxi or Grab from the airport; check the fare locally.
On the 27th the roads near the shrine may be closed. In 2016 a detour was announced from Quezon National Highway via Asangil Road to Punta Engaño Road.
From Cebu City, cross to Mactan Island by the Marcelo Fernan Bridge, the Mactan–Mandaue Bridge or the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway.
Traffic is heavy on event days, so leave earlier than usual.

Because the reenactment is on April 27, plan your travel dates around that day. The program and any holiday declaration differ from year to year. In 2016 it was declared a special holiday; I could not confirm whether one was declared for 2026.
April is Cebu's dry season, which suits outdoor events, but the midday sun is strong. Going early in the morning is best.

In 2023 the festival ran for the whole of April, and the food festival opened on April 21. Choose your visit by looking at the schedule. In mid-April there were a job fair, cooking competitions and a bazaar, and a street party was held on the night of the 27th.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Opening events and the food festival. Quieter than the reenactment.
The battle reenactment and ceremony. The busiest day, with road closures.
Remaining shows and closing events. Lodging rates return to normal.

Beach resorts on Mactan Island and hotels near the airport are closest to the shrine. April is peak season, so it is safer to book early for the days around the 27th. You can also commute from downtown Cebu, but traffic is heavy.

The food festival next to the shrine is the easiest place to eat. Dishes from resort restaurants and local eateries are served, and you can try local seafood and Cebu's grilled specialties. Menus and prices at individual vendors differ every year.

During the event the city holds a food festival that gathers dishes from hotels and resorts. In 2023, places such as JPark Island Resort and Marina Seaview held separate night events. Participating vendors change every year, so check the announcements to see who will be there.
The reenactment starts in the morning under strong sun, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
Roads near the shrine are closed, so arrive early or be ready to walk.
Check the event schedule in announcements from Lapu-Lapu City Hall or its tourism office.
Photography is fine, but do not get close to the actors or the stage.
Carry cash in small bills. Many booths do not accept cards.
Seeing the Mactan Shrine together with the statue in front of it helps you understand the history.
Mobile signal can weaken on the 27th, so save your route in advance.
During the festival, announcements from the Lapu-Lapu tourism office and City Hall on social media are the fastest. Plans can change or be cancelled.
In 2026 the street-dance competition was cancelled because of an energy crisis. The program changes every year.
The shrine area is crowded on event days and pickpockets are possible, so keep your belongings in front of you.
Taxis and Grab may be hard to find, or fares may rise.
Visits and speeches by officials can change the order of the program.
At food stalls, check hygiene and choose food that is freshly cooked.
Whether the day is a holiday differs by year. In 2016 it was a special city holiday, so downtown banks and government offices may be closed.
A national shrine built where the battle is said to have taken place, with the Lapulapu statue and the Magellan marker. The reenactment is also held on the beach in front of it.
A cross in downtown Cebu commemorating the arrival of the Spanish. See the history of how Christianity came to Cebu before the Battle of Mactan.
An island with beach resorts and dive operators, good for resting after the event.
Cebu's signature festival, held on the third Sunday of January. Compare it with Kadaugan to see Cebu's festival culture.
